name: SWIFT — Administrative or Attacker Tooling Executed on a SWIFT Server
description:
Attacker objective
Operate hands-on-keyboard on the SWIFT payment platform — running scripting interpreters, remote-execution utilities, credential-dumping or reconnaissance tooling — to stage fraud, dump credentials, or move laterally.

Detection logic
The SWIFT servers run a tightly-scoped set of payment and file-transfer processes. Execution of PowerShell, PsExec/WMIC remote-exec utilities, credential-dumping tools, or reconnaissance binaries on these servers is outside normal operation and indicates interactive attacker activity or malicious automation on a Tier-0 asset.

Why this detection works
Scoping process-creation events on the SWIFT servers to attacker/administrative tooling (excluding the platform's normal command and SFTP processes) surfaces hands-on-keyboard activity on the payment system.

False positives
A sanctioned administrator or vendor running a diagnostic script/tool during an approved maintenance window.

Tuning
Allowlist sanctioned maintenance tooling/windows; some environments run legitimate PowerShell/scripting in SWIFT automation — baseline and exclude verified scripts; prioritise credential-dumping and remote-exec tooling.

Required telemetry
Windows Security on the SWIFT servers: event.code 4688, process.name/process.executable, process.command_line (if enabled), SubjectUserName, host.name.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. process.name/executable = the tool; SubjectUserName = who ran it; host.name = the SWIFT server.
2. Confirm whether an approved maintenance was underway; PowerShell, PsExec, WMIC, procdump or recon tooling on a SWIFT server is high-risk — treat as a suspected intrusion and isolate/preserve.
3. Correlate with the interactive-logon and system-change detections on the same SWIFT server.
false_positives: A sanctioned administrator or vendor running a diagnostic script/tool during an approved maintenance window.
query: (host.name:*sw-app* or host.name:saa* or host.name:*swift*) and event.code:"4688" and process.name:("psexec.exe" or "psexesvc.exe" or "paexec.exe" or "wmic.exe" or "whoami.exe" or "nltest.exe" or "mshta.exe" or "certutil.exe" or "bitsadmin.exe" or "procdump.exe" or "procdump64.exe" or "ntdsutil.exe" or "vssadmin.exe" or "mimikatz.exe" or "rubeus.exe" or "sharphound.exe" or "adfind.exe" or "psloggedon.exe" or "netscan.exe" or "cobaltstrike.exe" or "advanced_port_scanner.exe")

name: SWIFT — New Interactive or Remote Logon to a SWIFT Server
description:
Attacker objective
Gain hands-on access to the SWIFT payment platform by logging on interactively or over RDP with a new or unauthorized account, to view or manipulate international payments.

Detection logic
The SWIFT servers are Tier-0 payment assets accessed interactively by a small, fixed set of administrators and monitoring accounts. An interactive (type 2), RDP (type 10) or unlock (type 7) logon by an account never seen before on the SWIFT estate is a high-risk access event.

Why this detection works
A new-terms model over the interactive/RDP logon account, scoped to the SWIFT servers and excluding known monitoring/system accounts, fires only when a genuinely new operator touches the payment platform.

False positives
Onboarding of a new authorized SWIFT administrator; a new monitoring/service account performing an interactive logon.

Tuning
Allowlist verified new SWIFT administrators after review; keep the monitoring-account exclusions current; treat any unexpected interactive logon to SWIFT as an incident.

Required telemetry
Windows Security on the SWIFT servers: event.code 4624, LogonType 2/7/10, TargetUserName, IpAddress, host.name.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. TargetUserName = the new account; host.name = which SWIFT server; IpAddress = source of the logon.
2. Confirm the account is an authorized SWIFT operator/admin and the access was expected; an unexpected interactive logon to SWIFT is a suspected fraud/intrusion event — escalate.
3. Review what the session did (process execution, config/system changes) on the SWIFT server.
false_positives: Onboarding of a new authorized SWIFT administrator; a new monitoring/service account performing an interactive logon.
query: (host.name:*sw-app* or host.name:saa* or host.name:*swift*) and event.code:"4624" and winlog.event_data.LogonType:("2" or "7" or "10") and not winlog.event_data.TargetUserName:("SolarWinds" or "NCM" or "*$" or "DWM-*" or "UMFD-*" or "SYSTEM")

name: SWIFT — Unauthorized System Change on the SWIFT Payment Server
description:
Attacker objective
Tamper with the SWIFT payment server — install a service, create/enable a local account, add an account to a privileged group, or clear the security log — to establish persistence or fraudulently manipulate international payments.

Attack logic
The SWIFT application server is a Tier-0 payment asset; any OS-level change to it (new service, new/enabled account, privileged-group addition, log clearing) outside authorized change control is high-risk and can enable payment fraud or hide it.

Why this detection works
Scoping Windows service-installation, account-management, privileged-group and log-clear events to the SWIFT server surfaces integrity-affecting changes to the payment platform; these events are rare or zero on this server in normal operation.

False positives
An authorized, change-controlled maintenance action on the SWIFT server.

Tuning
Allowlist scheduled maintenance windows and sanctioned admin service/account changes; correlate every hit with the change-management record; treat any log-clear (1102) or new privileged account as an incident until proven authorized.

Required telemetry
Windows Security on the SWIFT server: event.code 4697/7045 (service), 4720/4722/4738 (account), 4728/4732/4756 (group), 1102 (log cleared), host.name.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. host.name = the SWIFT server; event.code identifies the change (service install, account, group, log clear).
2. Verify against change management; a new service, new privileged account, or a cleared log on the SWIFT server is a suspected integrity/fraud event — escalate immediately.
3. Correlate with the acting account's logons and with any SWIFT application activity in the same window.
false_positives: An authorized, change-controlled maintenance action on the SWIFT server.
query: (host.name:*sw-app* or host.name:saa* or host.name:*swift*) and event.code:("4697" or "7045" or "1102" or "4720" or "4722" or "4732" or "4756" or "4728" or "4738" or "4719" or "4739" or "4964")
